title: Elodie and the Compass
premise: Jude Fairweather has spent years erasing themselves from maps, records, and family, digging where no one looks. When a dying prospector named Callum Voss trades them a hand-drawn map to the Hollow Compass—a relic that supposedly points to what its bearer most desires—in exchange for a promise to see it home, Jude inherits a treasure they never wanted and a debt they can't refuse. Hunted by Voss's former partners, who have already killed for a fraction of the truth, Jude must cross the Ashkettle Range ahead of the first snows, reluctantly gathering a found family of outcasts along the way. At the summit, Jude discovers the Compass is real but hollow: it grants nothing, only reveals, and the men pursuing it would rather burn the range down than leave empty-handed. Jude survives by giving the Compass away—dropping it into the glacier crevasse where Voss first found it—and returns not invisible, but known, keeping their promise by carrying Voss's letters to the daughter he abandoned.
about_author: W. M. Ravensworth is the pen name of a former field surveyor who spent a decade mapping remote ridgelines before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people the wilderness refuses to let go of, and they still can't read a contour line without feeling something.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dirt
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Working a black-market dig in the borderlands, Jude unearths a grave robbers' cache and walks away from it, establishing their skill and their refusal to want anything. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as armor. Ends with word that their estranged mother, archaeologist Dr. Imogen Fairweather, has published a paper mentioning a relic called the Hollow Compass.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Last Bargain
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A gut-shot prospector, Callum Voss, collapses at Jude's camp and trades a hand-drawn map for a promise: carry it across the Ashkettle Range and deliver his letters to a daughter in Merrow's Landing. He dies at dawn. Emotional beat: reluctant obligation. Jude burns nothing, keeps everything, and hates themselves for it.

chapters.title: Men Who Follow
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with a brief interlude from the hunter Dane Kessler. Three riders reach the border town asking about a dying man. Jude slips out the back with the map sewn into a coat lining. Emotional beat: the old invisibility failing. First appearance of the map's strange detail: the Compass is drawn at the center of a range that officially doesn't exist.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Sells Passes
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the staging town of Bracken Ford, Jude hires a guide: Sefa Ilin, a teenage smuggler who knows the range's unmarked trails and charges double for silence. Emotional beat: wary transactional trust. Sefa warns that the high passes close in nineteen days, and that someone else bought a pass west two days ago.

chapters.title: What Voss Carried
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Reading Voss's letters by firelight, Jude learns the Compass was found in a crevasse with three other men, only Voss walking out. The letters are unsent apologies. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger. Jude begins to understand the promise isn't about a relic—it's about a confession.

chapters.title: The River That Forgets
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The pair fords the Sere River at flood stage; Sefa nearly drowns, Jude pulls her out, and their partnership stops being transactional. Kessler's riders are spotted on the far bank. Emotional beat: first bond, first real fear. Sefa admits she's guiding them partly to escape a debt of her own.

chapters.title: The Company of the Broken
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At an abandoned waystation they find Odile Marchand, a disgraced cartographer whose maps were used to frame a massacre, and Tomas Reyes, a deserter medic. Neither will let the other travel alone. Emotional beat: the found family forming against everyone's will. The party of four becomes a party of five when a mule is involved.

chapters.title: Kessler's Offer
chapters.summary: Kessler's POV. Kessler catches Jude alone at a waterhole and offers a clean deal: the map, and no one gets hurt. He reveals Voss's former partners killed a fourth man for less. Jude refuses, lying that the map is already destroyed. Emotional beat: the corruption of power shown in miniature—Kessler genuinely believes he's the reasonable one.

chapters.title: The Switchback
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The party begins the ascent through the switchbacks, and Odile recognizes the terrain from her disgraced survey work—she helped map this range for the men now hunting them. Emotional beat: guilt and the price of complicity. She quietly alters their route to a pass she never sold, buying time and spending trust.

chapters.title: Storm on the Shoulder
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. An early storm pins the party on an exposed shoulder of the range; Tomas treats frostbite and a broken wrist, revealing he deserted after being ordered to let miners die. Emotional beat: the price of survival—everyone here has paid something. Jude tells the group the truth about the Compass for the first time.

chapters.title: The Hollow Village
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. They shelter in a village emptied decades ago by the same company Kessler serves; Sefa's family was among the displaced. Emotional beat: belonging and its theft. Sefa decides she's not guiding for money anymore—she's guiding to see what the company buried.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Saddle
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Reyes, offered amnesty for his family, slips away in the night with a copy of the map he made while the others slept. Emotional beat: betrayal that hurts because it's understandable. Jude chooses not to pursue, splitting the party's already thin margin of safety.

chapters.title: The Crevasse Field
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Crossing the glacier where Voss found the Compass, the party is ambushed by Kessler's men; Odile takes a bullet and the mule is lost with half the food. They shelter in the crevasse itself—the very one from Voss's letters. Emotional beat: survival at its most brutal and most tender.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, trapped overnight with the wounded Odile. Jude finds the niche where the Compass lay for years and, in the ice walls, older things: a rope, a boot, names scratched by the men who never walked out. Emotional beat: dread and clarity. Jude realizes the Compass was never a treasure; it was evidence.

chapters.title: Reyes's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. At Kessler's camp, Reyes discovers the promised amnesty is a lie—Kessler plans to kill him once the summit is reached. Reyes burns his copy of the map and walks back into the storm to warn the others. Emotional beat: a man choosing the hard right. He arrives half-frozen, carrying nothing but the warning.

chapters.title: The Last Ascent
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. With one day before the snows close the pass, the party climbs the final ridge—Odile on a litter, Reyes frostbitten, Sefa navigating by memory because the map burned with the mule. Emotional beat: exhausted resolve. From the summit they see the Hollow Compass site below: a ring of stones around a shaft, and Kessler's camp already there.

chapters.title: The Compass Turns
chapters.summary: Kessler's POV. Kessler's men breach the shaft and find the Compass—a needle of black glass that points, for each man who holds it, at the thing he wants most. It points each of them somewhere impossible, and they begin to turn on each other. Emotional beat: power consuming its seekers. Kessler holds it and it points at nothing at all.

chapters.title: The Summit of Wanting
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude descends into the standoff and takes the Compass from the chaos, feeling it pull toward Merrow's Landing—toward the mother who let them vanish. They understand at last what it reveals: not treasure, but the truth of what you've abandoned. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh. Kessler offers everything for it.

chapters.title: The Giving
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Climax. Rather than fight for it, Jude walks to the crevasse edge and gives the Compass back to the ice, in front of Kessler, his men, and the storm. The men's alliance shatters without the prize; Kessler, pointing his gun at Jude, is stopped not by force but by Sefa, Odile, and Reyes standing beside them. Emotional beat: power dies when no one wants it.

chapters.title: Descent Before Snow
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The party races down the east side as the first true snow falls, Kessler's broken men scattering behind them. They reach the treeline alive, all five, barely. Emotional beat: hard-won grace. Sefa realizes she's stopped running from her family's displacement and started carrying it.

chapters.title: Merrow's Landing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude delivers Voss's letters to his daughter, Mara, and stays for the answers—learning Voss walked away from the other three to save himself, and wrote letters he never dared send. Emotional beat: the price of survival, named honestly. Mara asks Jude to stay; Jude, for the first time, doesn't leave before dawn.

chapters.title: Known Ground
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, closing with a letter to Imogen Fairweather. Jude writes to their mother for the first time in years—not forgiveness, not yet, but coordinates, and an offer to dig something together. The found family wintering in Merrow's Landing, visible, named, and staying. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not stumbled into. The wilderness, Jude admits, was never the thing that hid them.
